title: Image of a pulled-back ideal-module product inclusion
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on $Y$, and $\mathcal G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $T=f^*$ be module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], $\mathcal I=\mathcal J\mathcal O_X=\mathcal J.\mathrm{comap}(f)$ the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and let $i:\mathcal J\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ and $k:\mathcal I(T\mathcal G)\to T\mathcal G$ be the canonical product inclusions [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Then $\operatorname{Im}(T i)=\operatorname{Im}(k)$ as subobjects of $T\mathcal G$ (images in the abelian category of module sheaves).

source.place: Lemma 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback), displayed quotient calculation; the image calculation in its right-exactness argument, expanded using Modules 01BG (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent) and Schemes 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: Fix f:X -> Y, J and a quasi-coherent G. Affine opens U of X over affine opens V of Y form a basis: for x in an open W choose affine V containing f(x), then affine U containing x inside W intersect f^{-1}(V).

The ideal-product theorem makes JG quasi-coherent. Tensor pullback is naturally isomorphic to the standard pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints to module pushforward (both adjunctions are the recorded module pullback adjunction); transport the standard pullback quasi-coherence instance. Thus TG and T(JG) are quasi-coherent. Apply the quasi-coherent image theorem to T(i_G): its image is quasi-coherent and, on an affine U, its sections inside TG(U) are exactly the range of T(i_G)_U. The same ideal-product theorem identifies the image of k_G on U with I(U) TG(U), where I=J.comap f. Reuse Scheme.image_range_affine, the proved private helper in AffinePushforwardIdealProduct, via a proof-only import all; it transfers the existing abelian image-section formula to chosen images. The affine pushforward theorem itself is not applied.

Put A=O_Y(V), B=O_X(U), rho=f.appLE, a=J(V) and M=G(V). The ideal-product formula identifies the range of i_G on V with aM. Use the natural A-linear affine pullback section comparisons for JG and G and their surjectivity to reduce the range calculation to pure tensors. The pulled-back morphism itself is B-linear, so its range Q is a B-submodule; the comparison scalar-compatibility clause and injectivity are not needed.

Put Q equal to the B-linear range of the pulled-back inclusion on U. Naturality and surjectivity of the affine comparison reduce Q <= I(U) TG(U) to pure tensors of sections of JG. The affine ideal-product formula puts every such section in J(V) G(V); induction on sums of products and the tensor balancing identity put its image in I(U) TG(U). Conversely, for a in J(V) and a section n of TG(U), lift n through the surjective affine comparison and induct on pure tensors. The section a*m is in the range of JG(V) -> G(V); a lift r supplies the preimage c_JG(r tensor b) of rho(a)*c_G(m tensor b). Induct on the ideal span defining Ideal.map to obtain I(U) TG(U) <= Q. The ideal_comap_appLE formula identifies I(U) with Ideal.map rho J(V). No flatness or injectivity of a tensor map is used.

The existing Scheme.image_range_affine helper transfers the equal section ranges of the two maps to their chosen image inclusions on paired affine opens U <= f^{-1}(V). To show either image subobject is contained in the other, compose its inclusion with the cokernel projection of the other. Its sections vanish on all paired affines by range containment. For any open W these paired affines inside W cover W: choose affine V about f(x), then affine U about x inside W intersect f^{-1}(V). Sheaf separatedness makes the composite vanish on W. Lift the inclusion through the kernel of the other cokernel projection (its abelian image), and invert the image factorization of the other monomorphism. This gives a factorization and therefore a subobject inequality. Antisymmetry gives the required equality.

lean.statement:
theorem modulePullbackIdealProductImage {X Y : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (G : Y.Modules) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) :
    imageSubobject ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).map
      (Scheme.idealModuleProductι J.toModulesι G)) =
      imageSubobject (Scheme.idealModuleProductι (J.comap f).toModulesι
        ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).obj G))
